relationships.subject: TET1
relationships.evidence_quote: Hence, spinal TET1 enhances BDNF transcription by promoting TET1-mediated demethylation and inhibiting DNMT-dependent methylation.

relationships.subject: DNMT3a
relationships.evidence_quote: These upregulations are associated with DNA methylation alteration at the Kcna2 promoter, leading to the epigenetic silencing of the Kcna2 gene, which encodes the Kv1.2 potassium channel.

relationships.subject: DNMT3a
relationships.evidence_quote: DNMT3a upregulation in the spinal cord [47] and DRG [59] following peripheral nerve injury also orchestrate the epigenetic silencing of the the mu-1 opioid receptor gene (Oprm1) gene

relationships.subject: MBD1
relationships.evidence_quote: This effect is likely due to MBD1’s suppression of Oprm1 and Kcna2 expression, potentially downregulating MOR and Kv1.2 proteins in nociceptive pathways

key_findings: Review of DNA methylation (DNMTs, TETs, MBD proteins) regulating nociceptive genes such as Kcna2, Oprm1 and BDNF in chronic pain.
DNA methylation reprogramming occurs early in the acute-to-chronic pain transition.
